headline: Milford's Liam advocates long-term investing principles — compounding and dollar cost averaging — as the foundation for KiwiSaver strategy over short-term market timing.
reasoning: Liam explains that compounding allows returns to generate their own returns over time, building growth on itself like a snowball. Dollar cost averaging means regularly investing and buying more units when prices are low and fewer when high, together smoothing out volatility. These benefits only materialise if investors stay invested, as chopping and changing erodes the compounding effect. Some funds are designed to manage risk across a full market cycle rather than chase short-term gains, meaning they may lag during strong rallies but protect capital during downturns, delivering better risk-adjusted results over time. Liam emphasises that investors should return to basics — investment timeframe and risk tolerance — rather than reacting to recent performance, as selling during a downturn can do more harm than good.
quote: Well, those principles are key to understanding why short term movements don't matter as much as people may think. So compounding, it just means that your returns generate their own returns over time. So growth builds on itself. Think of a snowball rolling down a hill getting bigger and bigger over the years. Dollar cost averaging on the other hand, that means you're regularly investing buying more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high. Together they help smooth out volatility and turn market ups and downs into an advantage over the long run. But these benefits only really show up if you stay invested. So chopping and changing in and out of the market erodes those benefits. So focusing on the long term is crucial.
